On Tue, Jun 11, 2028 at 08:12 AM Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Solstice's request. I have a redacted diagram and some notes but would appreciate your help on two things:
>
> 1) Grace — can you review the diagram (attached) and add a 1-page threat-model summary that covers the inference-path (prefix caching, sidecar, control plane) and recommended mitigations?

Attached is a short draft (threat-summary-draft.txt) and inline highlights below:

- Threat: Cross-tenant inference data exposure via KV cache reuse.
  Mitigation: Per-tenant cache namespaces, ephemeral TTLs, and cache zeroization on session termination. Residual risk: low if TTLs <= 2h and zeroization enforced.

- Threat: Sidecar compromise leading to request injection or exfiltration.
  Mitigation: Sidecars run in isolated containers with immutable images, mTLS to control plane, and strict egress policies; image attestation on deploy. Residual risk: moderate (attacker needs code execution on node).

- Threat: Control plane impersonation or rollout of malicious model variant.
  Mitigation: Signed model manifests, RBAC for rollout, canary deploys with traffic shaping, and automated rollback on regression signals. Residual risk: low-medium depending on supply-chain controls.

- Threat: Lateral movement via shared orchestration layer or GPU hosts.
  Mitigation: Tenant-aware scheduling, hypervisor/driver hardening, host-level microsegmentation; optional dedicated pools for high-risk tenants. Residual risk: medium.

I also recommend we call out: HSM-backed per-tenant keys (KMS integration), audit-log retention (13 months default, extendable), and encrypted KV at rest (AES-GCM) + TLS1.3 in transit.

Attaching the draft as requested. Irene, can you confirm the AES-GCM/KMS phrasing and whether we should mention key rotation cadence?

- Grace

Attachment: threat-summary-draft.txt (plain text, 1 page)

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the draft threat summary. A couple of clarifying items before we route to our auditors:

1) Sidecar communication: Can you confirm whether sidecar <-> control-plane uses mutual TLS with per-tenant identities (not shared certs)?
2) KV cache encryption: Is per-tenant data encrypted at rest within the cache layer, or is isolation enforced only by namespaces/TTL?
3) Audit logs: will the sample logs include request IDs and tenant identifiers we can map back to SIDs? (we understand redaction may be needed)

If possible, a single-line confirmation for each is great — auditors want explicit yes/no + one-line detail.

Tom

Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network segmentation and tenant separation evidence request — clarifications

Tom — quick clarifications below (auditor-friendly):

1) Sidecar mTLS and identity: Yes. Sidecars authenticate to the control plane using mTLS with per-tenant SPIFFE-style identities issued by our internal PKI. Certificates are short-lived (1 hour) and rotated automatically.

2) KV cache encryption: Yes. Cache entries are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM with keys provisioned via customer-scoped KMS keys (HSM-backed where requested). Namespaces + TTLs add defense-in-depth; we do not reuse cache namespaces across tenants and zeroize on session tear-down.

3) Audit logs: Yes — sample logs include request IDs, tenant identifiers (redacted in the public packet), timestamps, route and model version. Full logs are provided in an encrypted evidence bundle after DPA execution; sample csv attached (audit-logs-sample.csv).

If you'd like, Grace or Irene can join the sync to walk these points. I'll also upload the redacted evidence packet to the secure drive link and share credentials once legal confirms the DPA path.

Thanks —
Michael
